findings.title: Cleanup logs every batch at Error level, including successes, with full ID lists
findings.body: The new per-batch closures log at Error level on every batch, including successful ones. This applies to 'Annotations to clean by time' and 'cleaned annotations by time' here (lines 534 and 537), to 'Annotations to clean by count' and 'cleaned annotations by count' (554 and 557), and to 'Tags to clean' and 'cleaned tags' (576 and 579). Each message includes the full ID slice, which can be up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries (32767 in the new test). A large backlog therefore produces many very large error-level log lines per cleanup cycle, and error-based alerting will fire on routine success. The "err" field is also always nil at these points, because fetchIDs errors return earlier. These should be Debug-level, without the full ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string building when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: In the SQLite branch, `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` rebuilds the entire string on every iteration, so building an IN list of n IDs copies O(n^2) bytes. For the 32767-ID batch exercised by the new test, each id adds about 7 bytes, so the total copying is roughly 7*n^2/2, about 3.8 GB of allocation and copying per batch. This repeats for every batch of the cleanup loop whenever the batch size exceeds 999 on SQLite. Use strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt to build the list in linear time.

findings.title: Unrelated change: cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker interval is changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This is not mentioned in the PR description and has nothing to do with the annotation deadlock fix. It makes every cleanup job in this loop (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, old annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history with its row-limit enforcement) run about 10 times as often in production, adding continuous DB load. It looks like a leftover debugging change and should be reverted, or split into its own justified PR.

findings.title: IN list with one placeholder per ID can exceed MySQL's 65535 placeholder limit
findings.body: On non-SQLite databases the DELETE uses one placeholder per ID, and the batch size is the configured annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size. MySQL prepared statements are limited to 65535 placeholders, so a batch size above that makes the DELETE fail on every batch and stops cleanup. The previous LIMIT-based statement had no such limit. The only special handling in this diff is for SQLite. Either cap the batch size or chunk the IDs for this case.

findings.title: Subtest cleanup is registered after setup and assertions that can fail
findings.body: t.Cleanup is registered only after createTestAnnotations and the assertAnnotationCount/assertAnnotationTagCount calls (lines 116-118). Those helpers call require, which stops the test with FailNow. If any of them fails, the rows are never deleted, and every following subtest starts with leftover annotations and fails on counts, which hides the real failure. The cleanup should be registered before the data is created, as the previous top-level version did.
